244	skipped[1]{index,operation,reason}:
245	  3,search,budget_exhausted
246	```
247	
248	**This one is a major bump.** Today's `completed[2]: a,b` inline array becomes `completed[2]{index,operation}:`, so existing rendered output differs — the SemVer table calls that major, and the exact-output tests in `idempotency.rs` (AC-032, AC-033) and the `snapshot_partial_success_full` insta snapshot change with it. There is no external consumer to break yet, which is the cheapest moment this change will ever have.
249	
250	`exit_code()` is unchanged: `0` when nothing failed, `1` when anything did.
251	
252	### 5. `structured_content` and a published `outputSchema`
253	
254	`to_call_tool_result()` already builds `structured_content` from `render(OutputFormat::Json)`. Extend that JSON to carry the envelope:
255	
256	```json
257	{
258	  "body": "…",
259	  "sections": [
260	    {
261	      "name": "brief.symbols",
262	      "kind": "toon",
263	      "fields": ["name", "kind", "file", "line"],
264	      "rows": [["RetryPolicy", "struct", "src/retry/policy.rs", 14]],
265	      "returnedCount": 12,
266	      "totalCount": 40,
267	      "truncated": true
268	    }
269	  ],
270	  "budget": {
271	    "tokensUsed": 7412,
272	    "bytesUsed": 31208,
273	    "maxTokens": 8000,
274	    "truncated": true,
275	    "sections": []
276	  },
277	  "provenance": {
278	    "entries": [{ "label": "analyzer", "value": "rust-analyzer@0.3.2" }],
279	    "fingerprint": "b3f1c0d2e4a58691"
280	  },
281	  "hints": ["…"],
282	  "recovery": [],
283	  "isError": false
284	}
285	```
286	
287	Every key in that object is camelCase — `returnedCount`, `totalCount`, `tokensUsed`, `maxTokens`, `isError`. The rendered examples above are the specification of that, not an illustration of it: a third-party harness plugin reading this JSON without linking any Rust is a first-class consumer, and `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` on every envelope type is what keeps the spelling stable. Labels inside `provenance.entries` are caller-supplied strings and michi does not case-convert them.
288	
289	`sections`, `budget`, and `provenance` appear only when their slots are set. A response built entirely through today's API still emits exactly `body`, `hints`, `recovery`, `isError` — the four keys AC-004 pins — so that criterion needs its assertion rewritten from "exactly this set" to "exactly this set, plus the envelope keys whose slots were set", not deleted.
290	
291	The schema is published through the existing `schemars` feature: `Section`, `SectionBody`, `BudgetSummary`, `SectionCost`, `ProvenanceBlock`, and `ProvenanceEntry` derive `JsonSchema`, and the server declares the result as its tool's `outputSchema`. MCP makes conformance binding once a schema is declared — servers MUST return conforming structured results, clients SHOULD validate — which is the reason to publish one rather than leave the shape implicit. The token-budget caveat in [06-decisions.md](06-decisions.md) still applies: `outputSchema` enters the context window at `tools/list` time, so declare it on always-loaded tools, not on deferred ones.
292	
293	## The render path
294	
295	```mermaid
296	flowchart TB
297	    S1["Section — Toon"]
298	    S2["Section — Kv"]
299	    SN["Section — Text"]
300	    B["BudgetSummary"]
301	    P["ProvenanceBlock"]
302	    HR["hints / recovery"]
303	
304	    S1 --> AR
305	    S2 --> AR
306	    SN --> AR
307	    B --> AR
308	    P --> AR
309	    HR --> AR
310	
311	    AR["AgentResponse — N sections"]
312	
313	    AR -->|"render_text()"| text["sections in order, then budget:, provenance:, help[], recovery[]"]
314	    AR -->|"render(OutputFormat::Json)"| json["sections[], budget, provenance, hints, recovery, isError"]
315	
316	    text --> block["ContentBlock { audience: [assistant] }"]
317	    human["human_content()"] --> ublock["ContentBlock { audience: [user] }"]
318	
319	    block --> ctr["mcp::CallToolResult"]
320	    ublock --> ctr
321	    json --> ctr
322	    ctr --> wire["MCP tools/call JSON"]
323	```
324	
325	Everything below `AgentResponse` in that diagram already exists and is unchanged. `CallToolResult { content, is_error, structured_content }`, `ContentBlock.audience: Vec<Audience>` matching MCP's array-typed `annotations.audience`, the private `*Wire` structs that add the `"type": "text"` discriminator and nest `audience` under `annotations`, and `structured_content` parsed into embedded JSON rather than double-encoded — see [04-mcp-and-napi.md](04-mcp-and-napi.md). The gap is in what `AgentResponse` can hold, not in how it reaches the wire.
326	
327	## Where these types come from
328	
329	`Section`, `SectionBody`, `BudgetSummary`, `SectionCost`, `ProvenanceBlock`, and `ProvenanceEntry` are defined in `michi-core`. michi reaches outside its own workspace for none of them, and in particular it does not depend on `wisp-contracts`.
330	
331	That is a change from an earlier draft of this document, which imported `wisp_contracts::BudgetReport` and `wisp_contracts::Provenance` behind an optional `contracts` feature. michi publishes to crates.io first, so a michi release cannot name a crate that is not published yet — and a feature gate does not fix an ordering problem, since an optional dependency still has to resolve. The vocabulary argument that justified the import is sound and unchanged: `Provenance` and `BudgetReport` are meanings Wisp and monokl must agree on, and they belong in a permissively licensed crate for the harness plugins that cannot link AGPL code. What michi needs is not that meaning. It is the handful of numbers and strings a block renders, which is a smaller thing, and michi's own.
332	
333	The conversion lives in the consumer, which already links both sides:
334	
335	| Consumer | Holds | Converts into |
336	| --- | --- | --- |
337	| `wisp-output` | `wisp_contracts::BudgetReport`, filled by `wisp-context`'s per-section allocator | `BudgetSummary` |
338	| `monokl-agent` | `wisp_contracts::BudgetReport`, filled by its own `apply_budget` | `BudgetSummary` |
339	| both of the above | `wisp_contracts::Provenance`, read off the snapshot the batch ran against | `ProvenanceBlock` |
340	
341	Each conversion is a few dozen lines of field copying in a crate that imports contracts anyway. michi imports it in no build, and learns nothing about how a `Budget` is allocated, what a `WorkspaceFingerprint` hashes, or how `CapabilityPrecision` ranks.
342	
343	`michi renders a budget; it never computes one` is what makes that split hold. Under monokl `08 §7.5` there are two independent producers of a budget report — `monokl-agent` for the CLI and Wisp's `wisp-context` for a briefing — and michi is the only renderer both share. A renderer needs the numbers, not the allocator that produced them, so the numbers are all the envelope takes.
344	
345	**No new feature flag.** All six types are built from types michi already owns, so all six are always compiled and gate 2's small default dependency set is untouched — there is no dependency to gate. `render_json()` stays hand-built and `serde_json`-free: michi owns these shapes, so it emits their keys the way it emits every other key today, and the `budget` and `provenance` JSON keys appear in a default build. The `serde` and `schemars` derives ride the existing optional features and add nothing to the default.
346	
347	## Rules this envelope has to hold
348	
349	| Rule | Why |
350	| --- | --- |
351	| **Never fail closed on overflow.** Partial results, plus counts, plus a refinement hint. Never "no content is returned." | Serena's `find_symbol` returns nothing once `max_answer_chars` is exceeded, leaving the agent to guess a narrower query with no information about what it missed. Partial results plus `total_count` plus a hint naming the refinement operator is strictly more useful, and it is the behavior monokl already has. Wisp D-019 states the same rule for its MCP surface. |
352	| **No pagination cursors on tool results.** | MCP defines `cursor`/`nextCursor` only for list operations — `tools/list` paginates, `tools/call` results have no cursor field, and the 2026-07-28 release candidate does not add one. A cursor on a tool result is a private convention no client will honor. Truncation plus counts plus a hint is the signal that works. |
353	| **TOON for five or more uniform rows; KV for a single receipt.** | TOON's saving comes from stating field names once across many rows. Below roughly five rows the header costs more than the repetition it removes, and a one-item result reads better as `key: value` lines. `SectionBody` carries both so one response can mix them section by section. |
354	| **michi never reads its own TOON back.** | TOON is a rendering target. No render path parses it, and no consumer should: a caller that needs the data as data reads `structured_content`, which carries the same values already typed. Wisp states the same rule for itself. The round-trip parser exists to prove the renderer's output is grammar-valid in property tests, not as a data path. |
355	| **Sections render in insertion order.** | Ordering is a policy the caller measures (Wisp's Prism A/Bs it). michi renders what it was handed, in the order it was handed. |
356	
357	## The Wisp arrangement
358	
359	Wisp's `wisp-output` crate depends on michi through a **local path dependency during coordinated development**, and the publish order runs one way: michi publishes first, and Wisp is not published until michi has a versioned release compatible with Wisp's license and MSRV (Wisp D-006). michi's declared MSRV is `1.93`.
360	
361	Nothing in Wisp gates a michi release, and no consumer integration gates it either (see [ADR 4](../adr/0004-publish-before-consumer-integration.md)). michi publishes first so Wisp can integrate against a versioned dependency, then Wisp can publish its own package. A tagged Git dependency (`michi-core = { git = "…", tag = "michi@0.x.y" }`) remains useful during coordinated development.
362	
363	Licensing is settled, not open. michi is `FSL-1.1-MIT`, matching Wisp's upper layers and Lumen, and monokl carries the same license. With all three on `FSL-1.1-MIT`, the FSL-linking-AGPL redistribution conflict this section used to flag no longer exists.
364	
365	## What this is not
366	
367	**Not a Wisp type, and not a monokl type.** `Section`, `SectionBody`, `BudgetSummary`, and `ProvenanceBlock` name nothing from either domain, and michi's manifest names neither crate. Any orin-dx tool returning heterogeneous results in one call — a status command reporting several subsystems, a CLI answering a compound query — uses the same envelope, and a tool with one list still writes `items()` and never sees a `Section`.
368

content.text:
Entire has no open findings on the stack now. There was exactly one, and I fixed it and pushed. A re-review of the new head hasn't run yet, so that is not yet confirmed independently.

**What there was**
- **Open findings:** a single medium finding on #111, in `napi.rs`. It was the only open one across the six trails.
- **The other trails:** 397, 399, 401, 402 and 403 are for PRs you'd already merged (#110, #112, #113, #114, #115), so they report "no open changes" and nothing was left to address.
- **Dismissed:** nothing needed dismissing.

**The finding was valid.** NAPI accounting counted string bytes only, but each `items()` call now appends a section instead of replacing the rows. A loop of `Array(100000).fill([])` calls was charged about 65 bytes each while keeping about 2.4 MB each, so 1,000 calls retained roughly 2.4 GB in the Node process.

**The fix**
- **Charges:** `items()` and `kvItems()` now charge the storage they keep, on top of string bytes: a `Value` per cell, a row vector per row, and a `String` per field or key. The 64 MiB cap is cumulative.
- **Test:** it first failed because all 1,000 calls were accepted. It passes now, with rejection after about 27 calls. It also covers non-string cells.
- **Mutant:** setting the row charge to zero makes the test fail again, and it's reverted.
- **Checks:** `just fmt-check`, `just clippy`, `just typos`, `just test-rust` and the napi clippy all exit 0, as do the Node package's `pnpm install`, `build` and `test`. The one clippy failure on the way, a `&String` parameter, was mine and is fixed.
- **No new changeset:** the code is still unreleased and the existing one covers it.

**What I did in Entire**
- **Resolved:** I resolved the finding with a note stating what changed, before pushing, as you asked.
- **Pushed:** one commit (`bd3359f`) as a fast-forward to `feat/envelope-sections`, the branch behind #111.

**Cleanup for you:** I left a local worktree and branch, `napi-row-accounting`, which can be deleted. The Entire re-review of the new head is still pending, and the Entire check on #111 will show its result.

What should we tell michi, callisto, and caliper about our capabilities so they can adopt it?

I'm reading "michi" in your list as Monokl and Wisp, since michi is us. Each message below rests on what I verified earlier, and I haven't checked Caliper's or Monokl's code against 0.10.

**To all consumers: what we are and aren't**
- Lead with the response contract, not TOON. michi renders what a caller has already decided into agent-readable text, and gives one shape for the things every tool re-invents: sections, a budget report, provenance, per-op outcomes, truncation signals, hints, recovery steps, redaction and retry math.
- Don't oversell TOON. Measured: the same accuracy as JSON and Markdown, about 47% fewer tokens than pretty JSON and only about 8% fewer than a Markdown table.
- Availability: 0.9.0 is published today. The envelope ships in 0.10.0, which is not out yet (#116). It is pre-1.0, and a minor bump can break. The whole family moves in lockstep.
- Licensing: `michi-graph` is MIT. `michi-core` and `michi-pipeline` are FSL-1.1-MIT.

**Callisto**
- Stay on `michi-graph`. Ordering, layers, ready sets, closures, `Dag<K, E>` edge kinds and `ready_by_edge` are what it uses, and 0.10 changes nothing for it there.
- Nothing else is worth adopting. `callisto-model` is MIT and can't depend on FSL crates, `michi-pipeline` doesn't fit a synchronous plan, and its redaction, tail truncation and retry-after parsing differ from michi's.
- We'd like its feedback on graph API gaps. Token-shape redaction is the one real gap on our side, and it needs a second consumer.

**Caliper**
- Sections now express its nested, heterogeneous output (components, props, diagnostics, stats), and the truncation signal can replace its inline `...(+N)` marker. Its own escaping differs from michi's TOON 4.4, so we should compare against the same fixtures before it adopts anything. Keep its canonical JSON as the source of truth.

**Monokl**
- Its agent layer converts its budget and provenance types into `BudgetSummary` and `ProvenanceBlock`, and batch results use the index-carrying `PartialSuccess`. It must migrate off `render_toon()` (steps are in #114). Section names must be distinct, or the response renders a validation error.

**Wisp**
- `wisp-output` converts the same two types, and MCP responses should use `CallToolResult`. The published `outputSchema` is not built yet. Wisp's decision D-029 needs a published compatible release, which means 0.10.0.

Want me to turn these into a short capability sheet in `docs/` plus a draft migration PR for Monokl, once 0.10.0 is out?

# Shared brief: michi hardening trails (read fully)

Repo /Users/gabe/Projects/michi (Rust workspace; `michi-core` FSL, `michi-graph` MIT no_std, `michi-pipeline` async, NAPI shim in `packages/michi-node`, its exports in `crates/michi-core/src/napi.rs`). 0.10.0 is released; we are pre-1.0 and every consumer is our own repo, so **breaking changes are fine and legacy surface is removed, never shimmed**. Follow `AGENTS.md` and `PRINCIPLES.md`; ADRs and `docs/spec/06-decisions.md` record decisions you must not re-litigate (read headings first).
Four read-only audits produced the findings you act on: `/tmp/claude-501/audit-{architecture,security,rust-perf,duplication}.md`. Your trail names the finding numbers; read those entries (evidence, proposed change, "Not examined") and verify each is still true on current main before changing code. If a finding is wrong or already fixed, say so and skip it.

## Parallel trails, strict ownership (this is how we avoid conflicts)
Other trails run at the same time in other worktrees. Edit only files your trail owns. If your change forces a one-line call-site fix in a file another trail owns (for example `napi.rs`), make the minimal fix and say so in your report. Never reformat or reorganize files you do not own. If `git merge origin/main` brings conflicts in your files, resolve them keeping both sides' intent.
Trails: T1 envelope integrity (core model files, toon/ writers); T2 NAPI structure (`napi.rs` and `packages/michi-node`); T3 release-signing CI (`.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`, `.prototools`); T4 pipeline error redaction (`crates/michi-pipeline/src/error.rs`, `redact.rs`, `fuzz/`, trust-model docs); T5 docs/tests/CI hygiene (docs drift, new tests, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`); T6 pipeline observers.

## Flow (autonomous; never ask questions; decide and report the decision)
1. `git fetch origin && git checkout -B <your-branch> origin/main` (git network and cargo need `dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true` on that one command; use `$TMPDIR` for temp files; keep commands simple, no computed git arguments).
2. TDD: a failing test first, confirm it fails for the right reason, then fix. For every behavioral claim, break the code on purpose (mutant), watch the test fail, revert. Report the mutants.
3. Update docs/spec for anything you change (CI's "Spec first" job) and rustdoc for every pub item. Add one `.changeset/<slug>.md` for code changes (look at existing ones and `CONTRIBUTING.md`; package `michi-core` unless your change is elsewhere; start a paragraph with `Breaking:` when behavior or API breaks). No changeset for CI-only or docs-only changes.
4. Checks, judged by exit code only: `just fmt-check`, `just clippy`, `just test-rust`, `just typos`, plus `just check` once at the end, plus anything specific to your trail (Node: `pnpm build && pnpm test` in `packages/michi-node`; workflows: `actionlint` and `just zizmor`).
5. Commit (conventional, why-not-what; **no claude.ai session links, no Claude-Session trailer**), push, open a **draft** PR against main with a short plain body (what, why, how checked, what was not run, any decision you made). Never merge, never force-push, never push to main.

## Final message (<= 200 words)
PR URL; per-finding outcome (fixed / skipped with reason); decisions you made; checks with exit codes; mutants run; anything left or surprising.

Six trails are now running in parallel, each in its own worktree with strict file ownership. Nothing has landed yet.

| Trail | Branch | Model, effort | Owns |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **T1 envelope integrity** | `refactor/envelope-integrity` | Opus, high | the core response model files and the toon writers |
| **T2 NAPI structure** | `refactor/napi-structure` | Sonnet, medium | `napi.rs` (split into modules) and `packages/michi-node` |
| **T3 release signing** | `ci/release-signing-hardening` | Sonnet, low | `callisto-release.yml` and `.prototools` |
| **T4 pipeline redaction** | `fix/pipeline-error-redaction` | Sonnet, medium | `michi-pipeline` errors, `redact.rs`, `fuzz/`, the trust-model doc |

| **T6 pipeline observers** | `perf/pipeline-observers` | Sonnet, medium | observer and exec code in `michi-pipeline` |

**How I avoided conflicts**
- **File ownership:** each trail may edit only its own files. A forced call-site fix elsewhere is limited to the minimum and must be reported.
- **Shared brief:** all trails use `/tmp/claude-501/trail-brief.md` for flow, checks and constraints. Each also reads the specific audit findings that define its trail and re-verifies them against current main before changing anything.
- **Related work grouped together:** the model's integrity (private `Section` fields, derived roll-up, one reserved-key list, JSON and TOON writer dedupe) sits in T1. T1 is the only trail with Opus at high effort, because it's the design-heavy one.
- **T6 measures first.** If the stall isn't material it makes no code change and records the measurement as a docs-only PR. I'd rather it stop than add risk to the pipeline's crash-safety.

**Hiccup:** one launch (T3) failed from a git worktree-creation race, and I relaunched it. All six are now running.

**What's deliberately held back** until T1 reports, because they all touch the same core files:
- the legacy leftovers (`ToonOptions.hints`, `render_parts`, `empty_state*`, module naming)
- the API invariants (private fields on `DomainError`/`RetryConfig`, deleting `michi_core::Error`, composing `PartialSuccess` with `AgentResponse`)
- the response-render performance work (the 2,015-allocations-versus-3 fix and an `AgentResponse` bench)

I'll launch those as a second parallel group once T1's API is settled. After everything lands, I'd run one Opus review over the combined diff. Merging stays yours.
